records.text: Quartermaster Lymel manages general goods and supplies in Tranquillien. She sends a bill of lading through Sunwing and trusts his account that the rest of the shipment will follow overland, saying he has never failed her. She recognizes the Forsaken's support for the sin'dorei, though she bluntly calls them ugly and rotting.

Skymaster Sunwing is a dragonhawk master in Tranquillien who offers travelers a fast, safer route to Silvermoon for a modest fare. He presents flight as freedom and handles Lymel's supply delivery, agreeing to carry the bill of lading and later trusting her account that more goods will follow overland.

Arcanist Vandril coordinates the effort to reclaim Suncrown, Goldenmist, and Windrunner villages from the Scourge, directing attacks against the forces occupying each. He is eager to destroy the Scourge and reclaim Quel'Thalas, and treats the villages' recovery as a way to concentrate the defense on the Dead Scar and Deatholme. When he receives a long-awaited response from the regent lord, its warning of a dark presence in the Ghostlands hardly surprises him.

Apothecary Renzithen studies how the plague affects different creatures, focusing on the spines and marrow of murlocs that retain free will in undeath. He has also developed a restorative draught intended to rouse prisoners subjected to the Scourge's will-breaking poisons. Renzithen calls the draught one of his finest creations, though he warns of possible confusion, nausea, and temporary blindness. He expects his research to bring him recognition.

Magister Darenis is a magister in Tranquillien who sees the abandoned Sanctum of the Moon as a source of useful arcane resources. He sends help to recover crystallized essences from the creatures within. He also urges seasoned defenders to join the magisters’ offensive against Dar’Khan at Deatholme, citing their recent efforts against the Scourge.

Deathstalker Rathiel gives Tranquillien’s Scourge-clearing work a blunt, practical edge. He asks capable visitors to thin the mindless Scourge on the Dead Scar and says he will recommend those who prove useful. He also handles the wanted bounty for Knucklerot and Luzran, presenting their heads as proof for a reward.

Geranis Whitemorn is a spirit of Suncrown Village whose people’s ritual to summon and control Aquantion ended in betrayal and death. He seeks the wave-shaped medallions used in the rite, then calls for Aquantion’s destruction so his companions’ spirits can be freed and the dead avenged. He warns that the elemental’s wrath is unrestrained without their magic controlling him.

Farstrider Sedina works from the Farstrider Enclave, recruiting help to keep plague from spreading through the Ghostlands' wildlife. She starts with tainted ghostclaw lynxes, then calls for a continued hunt of more dangerous plagued beasts, including spindleweb lurkers and vampiric mistbats. Her assignments focus on containing the plague's threat to local wildlife.

Ranger Vynna is a Farstrider at the enclave who investigates Dar'Khan's past and plans. She directs a search for clues at Dawnstar Spire, then treats the recovered journal as valuable intelligence for Magister Kaendris to examine. Her work connects the Farstriders' field inquiries with the magisters' efforts against Dar'Khan.

At the Sanctum of the Sun in the Ghostlands, Magister Idonis presses for action against Dar'Khan, questioning Kaendris's delay. His campaign targets Deatholme's Scourge leaders and forces; as their strength wanes, he speaks of moving against more strategic targets. He also presents the effort as a joint sin'dorei and Forsaken fight.

In Tranquillien, Magistrix Aminel develops draughts from undead remains to strengthen the fight against the Scourge: rotting hearts yield physical enhancement, while spinal dust boosts magical ability. She provides samples in exchange for these materials and invites further supplies, making her a recurring source of anti-Scourge combat enhancements.

Apprentice Varnis was held among the captives at Deatholme, apparently kept in a drugged stupor. After the restorative draught is administered, he thanks his rescuer and says he thought he was going to die.
Apothecary Enith was held at Deatholme in a condition that left her unable to rise. After the restorative draught, she thanks her rescuer and regrets having left Silverpine Forest.
Ranger Vedoran, a Farstrider, was among the captives held in a drugged torpor at Deatholme. After the restorative draught, he thanks the person who helped him.

Ranger Lethvalin is a Farstrider who reports that a failed attack on the Shadowpine trolls at Zeb'Sora cost many lives. Valanna sent him to seek help while she and the lieutenant remained in danger; he is impatient with delays as he waits for aid.

Lieutenant Tomathren is a Farstrider officer who blames Ranger Valanna for the losses in the failed attack and insists his own orders were ignored. He expects a commendation, believes he deserves acclaim, and, confused and exhausted, says he wants to go home to Silvermoon.

Ranger Valanna is a Farstrider who blames Lieutenant Tomathren for rushing them into a troll fight without scouting, which she says caused devastating losses. She wants revenge on the trolls, asks for help, and has sent rangers to seek aid for the survivors.

Captain Helios is a Farstrider officer directing the Ghostlands campaign against the Shadowpine trolls. He calls for their numbers to be reduced and their weapons gathered for use against the Scourge, then sends rangers to assess the damage and prepare an attack. After Ranger Lilatha returns, he orders someone to tend her injuries and thanks those who brought her back.

Rathis Tomber runs a Trade Supplies shop in Tranquillien, supplying goods useful to the war effort. After ghouls force him to abandon a cart, he asks for help recovering the supplies; once they arrive, he opens for business and offers trade goods.

Dame Auriferous directs the blood elf campaign from Tranquillien, weighing the defense of the Ghostlands against the push on Deatholme. She refuses to commit troops against Dar'khan while enemies threaten the flanks, and presses for results despite unavailable Farstriders and limited aid from Silvermoon. With most lives at risk being blood elf, she will not spend them carelessly; she also seeks promised Forsaken reinforcements while Shadowpine trolls and Zul'Aman threaten the eastern border.

Magister Sylastor studies the ley-line nexus at An'telas, seeking arcane power for the blood elves' struggle against the Scourge. Night elf plans have taught him enough about their moon crystals to recognize An'owyn as a scrying threat and devise how to deactivate it. He regards their surveillance as dangerous while his people are surrounded by enemies.

Magister Kaendris brings arcane analysis to the blood elves' campaign against Dar'Khan. He investigates the traitor's journal and seeks the Stones of Light and Flame, Sunwell-imbued artifacts that may help defeat the Scourge. He welcomes cooperation with the Forsaken and recognizes that the Farstriders share the goal of defeating Dar'Khan, despite their differences with magisters.

Arcanist Janeda works at the Sanctum of the Sun and urges Idonis to stay calm and focused, expecting a fully productive sanctum to compel Silvermoon to send help. Janeda condemns the Scourge's treatment of prisoners at Deatholme and directs rescuers to Apothecary Renzithen for his restorative draught. Janeda also urges attacks while enemies are unprepared, invoking sin'dorei vengeance that neither forgets nor forgives.
A scout of Tranquillien.

Luzran is an undead abomination created by Dar'Khan. A Ghostlands bounty warns that Luzran is extremely dangerous and has been seen patrolling near the Howling and Bleeding Ziggurats. The bounty requires the head as proof for Deathstalker Rathiel. Combat abilities include Cleave and Knock Away.

Knucklerot is an undead abomination created by Dar'Khan. A Ghostlands bounty warns that Knucklerot is extremely dangerous and has been seen patrolling near the Howling and Bleeding Ziggurats. The bounty requires the head as proof for Deathstalker Rathiel. Combat abilities include Corrosive Poison and Tetanus.

Borgoth the Bloodletter is one of Dar'Khan's four named Scourge lieutenants in Deatholme, where the leaders command vast undead armies and rank immediately below Dar'Khan. In combat Borgoth uses Rend and Head Crack, giving this lieutenant a brutal close-range fighting style.

Jurion the Deceiver is one of Dar'Khan's four named Scourge lieutenants in Deatholme, where the leaders command vast undead armies and rank immediately below Dar'Khan. Jurion uses Shadow Word: Pain in combat, setting this lieutenant apart from the others named by Magister Idonis.

Masophet the Black is one of Dar'Khan's four named Scourge lieutenants in Deatholme, where the leaders command vast undead armies and rank immediately below Dar'Khan. Magister Idonis names Masophet among those leaders.

Mirdoran the Fallen is one of Dar'Khan's four named Scourge lieutenants in Deatholme, where the leaders command vast undead armies and rank immediately below Dar'Khan. Mirdoran uses Sunder Armor and Shield Bash in combat, relying on direct blows against opponents.

Deathstalker Maltendis directs work from Tranquillien during the Forsaken campaign in the Ghostlands. He treats the Underlight Mines as a strategic asset and wants Blackpaw gnolls driven out so ore can supply arms and armor. He also investigates the rising troll dead at the Amani Catacombs, suspecting Shadowpine oracles use juju in their reanimation rites. Around Advisor Valwyn, he trades sly smirks and lascivious winks, a private levity amid his duties.

High Executor Mavren leads the Forsaken presence in Tranquillien and advises on the campaign against Dar'Khan at Deatholme. He argues with Dame Auriferous for concentrating forces on the assault, even at the cost of lives, and sees Deatholme's bottleneck as a strategic weakness. He regards the Forsaken as backup to the blood elves, since Undercity is stretched thin by the Scourge.

Master Chef Mouldier trains cooks and sells cooking supplies in Tranquillien. Sent from Silvermoon City to prepare cuisine for Dame Auriferous, he complains about the lack of food and the Forsaken around him. He makes do with crunchy spider legs, herbs, spices, and arcane ingredients.

Eralan runs a poison business in Tranquillien, dealing in blinding, crippling, and lethal wares. She treats trouble as an opportunity: she fronts thieves’ tools for a promised cut of a valuable ring, then calls the recovery of a murdered archaeologist’s shrunken head a perfect job because the merchant will pay. Her manner is gruff, but an associate describes her as trustworthy.
Narina is a bowyer who sells goods and offers repairs in the Ghostlands.

Advisor Valwyn serves as an intermediary for Dame Auriferous, directing weighty matters to her and relaying information in private. She handles the grim Amani Catacombs investigation on the Dame’s commission. In dealings with High Executor Mavren and Deathstalker Maltendis, Valwyn reacts with visible disapproval and pointedly ignores them.

Magister Quallestis sent his apprentice Shatharia to gather Underlight ore for an experiment intended to uncover an advantage against the Scourge. When an adventurer brings the samples in her place, he calls her difficult to train and says he will speak with her, while thanking the adventurer for completing the delivery.

Apprentice Shatharia is collecting Underlight ore for the magisters, but gnolls have overrun the mines. She asks for help because she fears failing to deliver the samples to Magister Quallestis in time and facing the consequences. The ore can be found in the mine’s veins and carried by its gnolls.

A Farstrider ranger captured in the Amani Catacombs, Lilatha asks for help escaping and an escort back to Captain Helios. During the journey she gives directions, warns of a troll ambush, and reports back to Helios when she reaches the enclave.
A risen undead creature, the Creeper uses Decayed Strength against nearby foes.
A risen undead creature, the Hungerer uses Blood Leech when wounded. Deathstalker Rathiel names Risen Hungerers among the Scourge to be slain in the Dead Scar.
A risen undead creature, the Stalker uses Curse of Blood against nearby foes.
A Dreadbone Skeleton that strikes nearby foes.
An Arcane Devourer that drains mana from foes in combat.
An undead Dreadbone Sentinel that uses Shield Bash in combat.
An undead Deathcage Scryer that holds its position outside combat.
An undead Deathcage Sorcerer that holds its position outside combat.
An undead Gangled Cannibal that becomes enraged when badly wounded.
A beast known as the Mana Shifter that casts Drain Mana on nearby targets.
An undead Phantasmal Watcher that holds its position outside combat.
A Nerubian Scourge creature at Suncrown Village; the quest describes these enemies as spider-like, and this guard uses Poison in combat.
A Fallen Ranger among the mindless Scourge occupying Windrunner Spire; it uses Banshee Wail in combat.
A Deatholme Acolyte among the Scourge at Windrunner Spire; outside combat it casts Demon Skin.
A Stonewing Tracker that casts Stone Skin in combat.
A Deatholme Necromancer that summons a Dreadbone Skeleton while out of combat.
A Deatholme Darkmage that casts Shadow Bolt and Curse of Weakness in combat and may flee for help at low health.

A Nerubis Centurion is one of the Scourge forces at Deatholme. Magister Idonis names Centurions among the fortress’s undead hordes and calls for their defeat; this centurion can use Deadly Poison in combat.

An Eye of Dar'Khan is a spectral soldier fashioned by Dar'Khan in Deatholme’s Tower of the Damned. Magister Idonis describes these creatures as killing machines strengthened by the fortress’s dark magic and urges their destruction before the Scourge army grows. This one uses Curse of Agony in combat.
A Wailer is one of the undead occupying Deatholme, where Magister Idonis calls for the fortress’s forces to be defeated. In combat, a Wailer can unleash Wailing Dead.
A Gangled Flesheater is a creature found in the Ghostlands. It uses Spirit Decay in combat.
A Phantasmal Seeker is a creature found in the Ghostlands. In combat, it can strike with Mind Blast.
A Stonewing Slayer is a creature found in the Ghostlands. It can use Rend Flesh in combat.
The Quel'dorei Ghost is one of the high-elf dead haunting Goldenmist Village, whose former inhabitants the Scourge have turned against the living. When wounded, it can shimmer and become intangible.
The Quel'dorei Wraith is one of the high-elf dead haunting Goldenmist Village, whose former inhabitants the Scourge have turned against the living. When wounded, it can shimmer and become intangible.

At the lake in the Ghostlands, the Ravening Apparition is one of the drowned ancestors whose haunting cries recall a tragedy now mostly forgotten. It attacks nearby intruders by exposing their weakness.
At the lake in the Ghostlands, the Vengeful Apparition is one of the drowned ancestors whose haunting cries recall a tragedy now mostly forgotten. When badly wounded, it can become enraged.

Dar'Khan Drathir is an undead former elf who aligned himself with the Scourge and schemed against his own people. He sought to steal the power of the Sunwell and is believed to command Scourge armies in the Ghostlands. He treats challengers as insolent mortal fools, threatening slow, painful deaths and promising that Deatholme's ghouls will feast on their remains.
A Sentinel Spy operating at An'daroth, among the night elves camped at the old high elf ley-line nexus. The spy is one of the scouts identified in the night elf presence in the Ghostlands.
A Darnassian druid in the Ghostlands who uses Faerie Fire in battle and Healing Touch to aid an injured ally, supporting the night elf presence with druidic magic.
A Darnassian huntress among the night elves in the Ghostlands, identified by her role as a hunter.
A Sentinel infiltrator active in the Ghostlands. When frightened, the infiltrator attempts to flee.
A Blackpaw gnoll of the clan that overran the strategically important Underlight Mines in the Ghostlands. When badly wounded, it flees for help.
A Blackpaw scavenger of the clan that overran the Underlight Mines in the Ghostlands. It attacks at close range with Pierce Armor and flees for help when badly wounded.
A shaman of the Blackpaw clan that overran the Underlight Mines in the Ghostlands. It casts Lightning Bolt in combat.
An Arcane Reaver found in the Ghostlands. It fights at close range and uses Knockdown against nearby opponents.
A Shadowpine Ripper found in the Ghostlands. It uses Pummel against nearby opponents.
A Shadowpine Witch found in the Ghostlands. In combat, it protects itself with Lightning Shield.
A mummified undead headhunter found in the Ghostlands. When it dies, it releases a Cloud of Disease.
A Shadowpine Oracle that casts Dark Offering when a friendly unit is near death and flees for help when badly wounded.
One of the Shadowpine forces Farstrider Solanna's volunteers are asked to reduce during the campaign against the troll camps.
One of the stronger Shadowpine trolls at Zeb'Nowa, the Catlord summons a Ghostclaw lynx and casts Bloodlust on a friendly unit that lacks it.
A Shadowpine Hexxer among the stronger trolls at Zeb'Nowa, using Hex and Dispel Magic in combat.
A starving Ghostclaw beast.

A Ghostlands lynx encountered in the area around the Farstrider Enclave. Farstrider Sedina identifies Ghostclaw Lynxes among the local wildlife tainted by the plague; this lynx can rake and claw when engaged.

A larger Ghostlands lynx, found around the Farstrider Enclave and Andilien Estate. Apprentice Vor'el identifies Ghostclaw Ravagers as hostile wildlife obstructing the planned advance outpost; a ravager can exploit an opponent's weakness when close.
A small spider of the Ghostlands. It can poison creatures that come within reach.

A more dangerous spindleweb spider of the Ghostlands, hunted west of the Dead Scar as part of Farstrider Sedina's effort to curb the plague among local wildlife. It can poison creatures that come within reach.

A greater spindleweb of the Ghostlands, counted among the hostile wildlife Apprentice Vor'el wants cleared from the area west and south of Andilien Estate for a planned advance outpost. It can poison creatures that come within reach.

Mistbats are clever Ghostlands hunters found south of the Elrendar River, where they prey on travelers. Their hunting combines a dragonhawk’s swiftness with a springpaw’s ferocity; a taming task describes befriending one.
Vampiric mistbats are among the more dangerous plagued wildlife south of the Farstrider Enclave in the Ghostlands. They attack with Draining Touch.
Lesser Scourgebats are found in the Ghostlands around the Dead Scar. They use Disease Touch in combat.

Anok'suten is a Nerubian leader who wanders Suncrown Village. A dying blood elf sent to fight the Nerubians revealed Anok'suten's role and asked others to bring help. Anok'suten strikes witheringly and uses poison.
Kel'gash the Wicked is the chieftain of the Shadowpine trolls, sought in a bounty notice at the Farstrider Enclave. The notice places him somewhere south in Zeb'Nowa and calls for his head.
An undead Grimscale that fights intruders and flees for help when badly wounded.
An undead Grimscale that stays still and stops attacking while out of combat.

A Farstrider at the Enclave, Krenn'an sees the drowned spirits in the northern lake as his ancestors and wants their suffering ended. Their tragedy is mostly forgotten, though their cries keep its curse present to him. He remembers the land beyond the lake as green and full of life.

A Farstrider at the Enclave, Solanna oversees the campaign against the local Shadowpine under orders from the captain. With resources stretched thin, she uses volunteers to keep the trolls off balance before a larger offensive. She sends help first against Zeb'Tela, then against the more powerful trolls at Zeb'Nowa, and hopes the pressure will give the Farstriders room to build their forces. She is also concerned that the Scourge and Zul'Aman-backed trolls divide the defenders' attention.

Apothecary Venustus is a Royal Apothecary Society apothecary temporarily loaned to the Farstriders to address their Shadowpine troll problem. He proposes poisoning the trolls’ food at Zeb’Nowa and takes evident pride in his work, eagerly pursuing a mixture even when one experiment fails. He hopes the attack will ease pressure on the Farstriders and let him return to Tranquillien.

A Shadowpine Shadowcaster is a hostile troll combatant encountered at Zeb’Tela. Farstrider Solanna identifies Shadowcasters as part of the local force the Farstriders are trying to weaken; in combat, this caster uses Mind Flay and Mark of Shadow.

Apprentice Vor’el is a magister’s apprentice at Andilien Estate, where Kaendris has sent him to clear hostile wildlife ahead of plans for an advance outpost against the Scourge. Vor’el openly delegates the dangerous work and admits he dreaded entering woods so close to Deatholme. He suspects apprentices receive the magisters’ most dangerous assignments, a concern that shapes his view of his place in their service.
Provisioner Vredigar serves his town amid equipment shortages. He says scarce equipment is reserved for people the town trusts, and that greater renown opens access to more goods.
The Ghostlands Guardians serve as sentries in the Ghostlands. Their name and presence across the region mark them as local protectors.
Innkeeper Kalarin offers what shelter is available in the shattered lands. As an innkeeper, Kalarin provides lodging and goods to visitors.

The dying blood elf was sent to fight Nerubians. As they lie dying, they tell the player that Arcanist Vandril did not know the Nerubians had a leader, identify Anok'suten, and point toward Suncrown Village, where she wanders.
Farstrider Dusking gives visitors a brief direction: speak with Farstrider Solanna if they have not already done so.
Paniar is a stable master who offers care for animal companions through the stables.
A humanoid Sentinel Leader in Ghostlands.

Keltus Darkleaf is a scout operating undercover near the night elf settlement of An'daroth. He reports that he has been surveying the night elves but has not been sending his findings. He says he intends to use his faithful Whisper as a first strike against sentinel spies, guided by the scent of a personal item. He distrusts an unknown visitor at first and tests them with a covert theft before entrusting them with his report.

Whisper is Keltus Darkleaf's faithful animal companion, whom he plans to send ahead against sentinel spies. He intends to guide her by the scent of a personal item taken from their leader, making Whisper part of his covert work around An'daroth.
Blacksmith Frances is a blacksmithing-supplies vendor in the Ghostlands. She welcomes visitors looking for supplies and offers goods for browsing.
Heron Skygaze sells food and drink in the Outland settlement. Her stock includes fresh meat, fish, mushrooms and drinks.
Terellia is a trade-supplies vendor in the Ghostlands. Visitors can browse her goods.

Dr. Whitherlimb is a violent creature who treats victims as sources of parts for his abominations. In combat he calls for fresh parts, and after a kill he describes the victim's brain or organs as useful donations.

Budd Nedreck is an ambitious treasure hunter organizing a crew to explore Zul'Aman. He boasts of fame and past exploits, and treats failed expeditions as an opportunity to continue his search for its treasures.
Provisioner Ameenah sells reagents and has little patience for Mack's drunken advances. She repeatedly orders him away, once threatening that Budd will feed him to her hounds.
Turgore is a humanoid found in both the Ghostlands and Northrend.
Catlord Corpse is found in two areas of the Ghostlands.
Mack eagerly awaits his long-overdue share of the spoils. He greets Ameenah with effusive admiration and persists after being rebuffed, promising to return in hopes that she will change her mind.
Samir is a merchant offering goods for visitors to browse.
Garg is a humanoid associated with the Ghostlands and Grizzly Hills.
Kurzel sells food and drink and is exasperated with Turgore’s laziness. Kurzel orders the peon to help unload and threatens to put something in his grog that he will never wake from.

Prigmon is a skinner helping Budd refine a forest-troll disguise, though pulling tusks makes him queasy. He asks for tusks to finish the disguise. He also wants his cousin Zungam rescued from Zul'Aman, admitting that debt is part of his concern and that he would otherwise leave him to his fate.

Brend's exchanges with Marge pair her requests for sweet talk with his complaints about being interrupted while drinking and a cutting joke that he cannot drink her pretty. He also tells Morgom that Marge needs attention.
Marge asks Brend to make eyes at her and whisper something sweet, but complains that he is always drinking. She reacts indignantly in their exchanges and addresses Morgom as a “filthy orc.”
Morgom is a humanoid who greets others with “Zug Zug!”

Donna Brascoe is an undercover investigator for the Shattrath Peacekeepers, sent to infiltrate Budd's gang. She says the adventurer was a person of interest in her investigation, but that their deeds cleared suspicion; she cites Zul'jin's defeat in explaining her commendation.
Budd’s Bodyguard is a combatant assigned to protect Budd, using a ranged shot and a net against nearby enemies.
The Ghostlands Flame Keeper tends the Ghostlands’ Horde festival flame. Its greeting encourages honoring Horde fires and voices hostility toward Alliance fires, urging their desecration.
The Rotting Crawler is a low-level beast found in the Ghostlands.

place_records.text: You are in Ghostlands, Horde land in the Eastern Kingdoms. Tranquillien is the main Horde town, and Hatchet Hills is held by neither side. The Scourge holds Deatholme and roams the Dead Scar, while mistbats, lynxes and plagued beasts prowl the wilds, and Shadowpine trolls make trouble at Zeb'Sora across the lake.

You are in Tranquillien, a Horde town in the Ghostlands. It has an inn, a flight master and a dragonhawk master, Skymaster Sunwing, who offers fast flights to Silvermoon. Quartermaster Lymel keeps the supply stores, and Deathstalker Rathiel recruits capable visitors to thin the mindless Scourge on the Dead Scar.

You are in Suncrown Village in the Ghostlands, a village the Scourge occupies. Nerubians guard its ruins, and their leader Anok'suten is said to wander here. The spirit of Geranis Whitemorn, a Suncrown elf, still lingers among the ruins, and Arcanist Vandril of Tranquillien is working to take the village back.
You are in Goldenmist Village, a Scourge-occupied village in the Ghostlands. Quel'dorei wraiths and ghosts haunt its ruins, and Arcanist Vandril in Tranquillien is directing efforts to reclaim it.

You are in Windrunner Village, one of the Scourge-occupied villages in the Ghostlands. Phantasmal seekers and stonewing slayers prowl among its ruins, and Arcanist Vandril in Tranquillien is directing efforts to reclaim it.

You are in the Sanctum of the Sun, a rebuilt Horde arcane sanctum in the Ghostlands. Magister Idonis presses an offensive against the Scourge at Deatholme, and Magister Kaendris studies the traitor Dar'Khan's journal and seeks the Stones of Light and Flame.

You are in the Sanctum of the Moon, a ruined arcane sanctum west of Tranquillien. Arcane devourers and mana shifters inhabit it, and Magister Darenis in Tranquillien sends for the crystallized essences its energies have produced.

You are in Dawnstar Spire, a tower in the Ghostlands northeast of the Farstrider Enclave where Dar'Khan once hid and schemed. Arcane reavers haunt it, and searches here have turned up Dar'Khan's journal.

You are in the Farstrider Enclave, on the southern shore of Lake Elrendar in the Ghostlands. Farstrider Sedina recruits help against the plague in the region's wildlife, and Ranger Vynna investigates Dar'Khan's past. It has repairs and a vendor. Vampiric mistbats still fly nearby.
You are in An'daroth, the old high elf ley-line nexus in the Ghostlands, where Alliance night elves have camped. A Sentinel spy works here among them, and a Sentinel leader is also present.
You are in An'telas, a ley-line nexus in the Ghostlands that Horde magisters study. Magister Sylastor is working to shut down the night elf moon crystal at An'owyn, which he sees as a scrying threat.

You are in Deatholme, the Scourge fortress of the traitor Dar'Khan in the Ghostlands. Eyes of Dar'Khan, nerubis centurions and necromancers fill its halls, and the Scourge keeps prisoners there in a drugged stupor.

You are in the Howling Ziggurat, one of the twin ziggurats in the middle of the Dead Scar, where the Stone of Light and the Stone of Flame were once thought to be held. Deatholme darkmages and stonewing trackers guard it, and Knucklerot, whom Tranquillien has put a bounty on, has been seen here.

You are in Shalandis Isle, a Ghostlands island where Alliance night elves keep a presence. A Darnassian druid and a Darnassian huntress are stationed here, and the druid mends injured allies with healing magic.

You are in Underlight Mines, a Horde mining site in the Ghostlands. Magisters send apprentices here for Underlight ore, but Blackpaw gnolls have overrun the mines. Apprentice Shatharia is gathering the ore and fears failing to get her samples to Magister Quallestis at the Sanctum of the Sun in time. Blackpaw gnolls, shamans and scavengers still roam the tunnels.

You are in Andilien Estate, a Horde holding in the Ghostlands where the magisters plan an advance outpost against the Scourge. Apprentice Vor'el was sent here by Magister Kaendris to clear the hostile wildlife, and vampiric mistbats are among the dangers.

You are in Hatchet Hills, a neutral camp in the Ghostlands where Budd Nedreck is gathering a crew to search Zul'Aman for treasure. Donna Brascoe, an undercover Shattrath Peacekeeper, is infiltrating his crew, and the skinner Prigmon is working on a forest-troll disguise for them. The camp has a flight master, repairs and a vendor, and there is a flight point at Zul'Aman.

You are in Sungraze Peak, a Horde-held ridge in the Ghostlands. Trolls captured the Farstrider ranger Lilatha in the Amani Catacombs. Mummified headhunters, starving ghostclaws, Shadowpine oracles and mistbats roam the peak.
You are in Zeb'Sora, a stretch of the Ghostlands. Shadowpine rippers and witches are the danger here.

You are in Lake Elrendar, Horde ground in the Ghostlands. Captain Helios directs the Farstriders' campaign against the Shadowpine trolls from the Farstrider Enclave, and Farstrider Solanna oversees the harassment of their camps. Apparitions haunt the northern lake, which Ranger Krenn'an sees as the drowned spirits of his ancestors. Apothecary Venustus, loaned from the Royal Apothecary Society, is developing poisons for the troll campaign.
You are in The Dead Scar, a Ghostlands area where risen hungerers, risen stalkers and dreadbone sentinels roam, along with gangled cannibals and dreadbone skeletons.

You are in Elrendar River, a Horde-held stretch of the Ghostlands near the night elf settlement of An'daroth. The Horde scout Keltus Darkleaf works undercover here, surveying the night elves, with his faithful animal companion Whisper. Arcane devourers, mana shifters and mistbats are the dangers.
You are in Zeb'Tela, a Ghostlands area where Shadowpine trolls keep camps. Headhunters and shadowcasters are the main danger.

You are in Zeb'Nowa, in the south of the Ghostlands, where the stronger Shadowpine trolls make their home. Catlords and hexxers are the main danger, and their chieftain Kel'gash the Wicked is said to dwell here.
You are in the Isle of Tribulations, a Ghostlands island where nerubis guards are the danger.
